content.text: {"grade": 4, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The core of the lower bound (Lemma 4) — the tree-component/signed-sum claim — is asserted with 'standard; details omitted', leaving the crux of Liu's guarantee unproved.", "errors": [{"description": "Lemma 4's essential step is not proved. One must observe that the number of pairs (edges) is at most n < n+1 vertices, hence some component is a tree/isolated vertex, then use its bipartition to sign the pieces. None of this counting or construction appears; the existence of V_T and signs with |\u039e| \u2264 \u03a3\u03b5_i + [M odd]a_M is simply asserted.", "quote": "By a tree-component argument on the multigraph whose vertices are the original pieces $0,1,\\dots,n$ and whose edges are the pairs $P_i$, there is a set $V_T\\subseteq\\{0,\\dots,n\\}$ and signs $s:V_T\\to\\{\\pm1\\}$ such that the signed sum $\\Xi:=\\sum_{j\\in V_T}s(j)\\,q_j$ satisfies $|\\Xi|\\le\\sum_i\\varepsilon_i+[M\\text{ odd}]\\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted)."}, {"description": "Supporting evidence for the omitted lemma is numerical (Monte Carlo / grid search), which carries no proof weight; the write-up leans on it in place of the missing argument.", "quote": "plus 40000-trial Monte Carlo for Lemma 4 and 4000 exact-arithmetic random tests of the Lemma 5 construction"}], "notes": "Answer and reduction are correct; Lemma 2 (picking phase) and Lemma 5 (upper bound construction, including the mark count \u2264 n and the pairing argument) are carefully and correctly proved. Only the lower-bound core is missing."}
